governance.note: All active levers trace to measured inputs. The new lever is a per-year MEASURED marginal-heat-rate anchor on MISO's SPP NeighborInterface (hr_by_year={2023:9.24, 2024:10.65, 2025:7.7}), derived by scripts/derive_neighbor_hr_by_year.py --iso MISO from SPP's OWN realized RT LMP (data/raw/_validation-source/actual_lmp_hourly_SPP.parquet) / Henry Hub x the load-shape convexity K — i.e. SPP's realized implied market heat rate each year, the same method already used for the PJM neighbor. Measured neighbor price-formation input (rule #12; forward analogue = the structural marginal_heat_rate when a year has no measured LMP); the derivation never sees MISO's own interchange flow (rule #11). The flat 10.0 over-priced the wind-heavy SPP hub in dear-gas 2025 (measured 7.7), making MISO look cheaper than SPP and flip to a fake net EXPORT; the cheaper measured SPP restores the correct net-import direction. Other measured levers (all on current main, unchanged): PJM neighbor per-year HR anchor, EIA-923-derived NUCLEAR_MONTHLY_CF refueling availability, priced import/export node via the reference-price interface, Manitoba firm-hydro import block, per-plant CAMPD tranche binning, historic CAMPD unit-outage windows (exogenous availability), measured F923 per-plant monthly delivered fuel, EIA-923 biomass must-run. Benchmark: this bundle's eia930 carries the EIA-930 'Other Fuel Sources' (NG: OTH) series, so the class-tolerance ACTUAL applies the generalized geo/biomass fold-in deflation (MISO ~12.8 of 15.5) — the model gas is scored against true natural gas, not the inflated NG cell. No adder/haircut/sigmoid tuned to the price or volume residual; no unit pinned to its observed output; no input rescaled so the model lands on actuals.
governance.results_note: Net interchange (EIA sign, + = export): 2023 model -71.9 vs actual -37.9; 2024 -49.8 vs -23.1; 2025 -6.7 vs -19.0. The SPP anchor FIXES the 2025 export-flip (miso10 was +3.4 net export -> now -6.7 net import, correct direction; import-hours 45.8->52.9% toward 79.2%; duration RMSE ~3600->2049) and slightly improves 2024 (52.3->49.8). It WORSENS 2023 over-import (69.3->71.9): the measured 2023 SPP HR (9.24) is cheaper than the flat 10.0, so MISO imports more — kept on faithfulness grounds (rule #1/#11; the measured price is correct). This isolates the REMAINING dominant miss as the import-node LEVEL / interface deliverability (the model systematically over-imports because cheap seam imports undercut the next domestic unit, unmasked further by the nuclear derate), NOT the per-year seam pricing. NOT calibrated yet.
governance.open_misses_note: Documented open structural misses (next levers, not residual fits): (1) systematic net OVER-import all years (2023 71.9 vs 37.9 the worst) — the import-node level / SPP+South interface deliverability limits (real MTEP/OASIS TTC vs the placeholder), the dominant remaining lever; (2) 2025 coal over-run (231.7 vs 192-201) persists though reduced — a dear-gas-2025 coal-offer/merit question, AFTER the import level is fixed; (3) CT_PEAKER real merit under-gen (model ~3 vs ~17-19 GT/IC) — recovers once imports stop undercutting + a scarcity tail forms (ORDC), NOT an offer fit; (4) scarcity tail absent (0 h >$200 vs 30/37/88). South/SOCO seam kept structural (no organized-market LMP).
